# Evaluation matrix

Which agents the skill supports, and what has been measured with each.

## Status definitions

- **Supported**: an install artifact exists in this repo. Nothing has been measured.
- **Tested**: at least one committed run produced plans with this agent + model.
- **Experimentally evaluated**: a committed run with ≥ 5 prompts, ≥ 3 runs per
  (prompt, condition) cell for a skill condition and a control, blinded judging by ≥ 1 judge
  model different from the generator, a summary with confidence intervals, and skill plans that
  could read the skill's files.

Statuses are computed from the committed evidence by `eval/dfa_eval/matrix.py`; none is declared
by hand.

Runs counts the plans a row's evidence produced. Measured result quotes mean differences
(treatment − control) with 95% t-intervals across prompts from the run's summary.json: adherence
is methodology adherence, scored with the skill author's own rubric, so a high value for plans
written with the skill is expected by construction; EQ is an LLM judge's engineering-quality score
of the written plan, not of outcomes. Read each run's REPORT.md for the caveats.

## Install artifacts (skill version 2.1.0)

| Agent | Artifact | Install | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `SKILL.md + reference/` | `python3 -I "$t/$f" --agent claude-code` | The installer (release asset install-dependency-first-architect-vX.Y.Z.py, run by the README's checked download block) writes the skill package to .claude/skills/dependency-first-architect/ in the project, or ~/.claude/skills with --global: SKILL.md, the reference files it loads on demand (plan template, validation examples, AI layer, layer map) and LICENSE. The same files are the release zip. Invoke with /dependency-first-architect or let the description trigger it. |
| Cursor | `adapters/cursor-dependency-first-architect.mdc` | `python3 -I "$t/$f" --agent cursor` | Generated from SKILL.md by build.py (alwaysApply: false, so it loads when a request matches) with the reference files appended as appendices; the installer writes it to .cursor/rules/dependency-first-architect.mdc. Also a release asset of the same name, for a manual install. |
| Codex | `adapters/codex/dependency-first-architect.md` | `python3 -I "$t/$f" --agent codex` | The installer writes the whole skill, reference files appended, to .codex/dependency-first-architect.md, and a ~1 KB block (adapters/codex/AGENTS-snippet.md) into AGENTS.md that tells Codex to read it when a request matches; the rest of AGENTS.md is kept. Not yet tested in Codex. Manual alternative: the release asset codex-AGENTS.md (adapters/AGENTS.md), the method without its reference files, read in every session (about 16 KB). |
